title: CLSI C62-A (1st edition, 2014) — as summarised by Lynch, Clin Chem 2016

source.citation: Lynch KL. CLSI C62-A: A New Standard for Clinical Mass Spectrometry. Clin Chem. 2016;62(1):24-29. doi:10.1373/clinchem.2015.238626 (Table 1)
source.document: CLSI C62-A, Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Methods; Approved Guideline, 1st edition (October 2014)
caveats: Secondary source: these criteria come from a published summary table, not from the CLSI document itself.
C62-A was replaced by the 2nd edition (June 2022) and the 3rd edition (June 2026). Check every criterion against the edition your laboratory holds before relying on it.
C62-A leaves several acceptance limits to the laboratory (trueness, QC, matrix effect within total allowable error). Those are marked lab_defined and have no default value on purpose.

terminology.LLMI: Lower limit of the measuring interval (formerly LLOQ)
terminology.ULMI: Upper limit of the measuring interval (formerly ULOQ)
terminology.note: C62-A calls 'verification' what FDA and EMA call 'validation'.

approaches.description: Comparison to a reference measurement procedure
Analysis of commutable certified reference materials

design.approaches_rule: more than one approach (the source says '>1')

criteria.basis: biological variation, clinical guidelines from expert groups, local or regional regulatory requirements

levels.definition: at and within 25% of any medical decision point

criteria.basis: goals may be tightened from total allowable error, biological variation, expert guidelines or regulation

design.samples: 3-5 different samples close to the predetermined limit

design.comparison: peak area of analyte spiked post-extraction vs analyte in neat solution

criteria.basis: evaluate within the total allowable error for the analyte

design.description: High concentration of each potential interferent in matrix (preferably a patient sample), with and without analyte

criteria.description: Interferent must not alter the calculated concentration

criteria.relative_to: mean ion ratio of the calibration standards

design.description: Extracted negative samples injected after samples with increasing analyte concentrations

criteria.description: Highest concentration that does not carry over to a negative sample at >= 25% of the LLMI

experiments.name: Stability
references: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation (recommended stability experiments)

design.comparison: extracted samples vs unextracted standards representing 100% recovery
design.endogenous_analytes: standard additions when the matrix is not blank

criteria.description: Analyte and IS recovery consistent, precise and reproducible

design.matrix: same biological matrix as the samples
placement: medically relevant decision points within the AMI

criteria.description: Any detected nonlinearity assessed for clinical significance
